svg.title: Crawling — okfy algorithm explainer
svg.desc: How one entry file becomes the set of concept files. The crawl starts at the file named by the start parameter, resolved against the bundle folder, and falls back to index.md when that parameter is absent, points at another origin or points outside the folder. A depth parameter caps the prefetch in link hops, and absent, all or inf means every level. The start is checked against the bundle root before anything is queued, so a start outside it ends the crawl at once with nothing loaded. The queue is a map from URL to entry plus an array of entries, with the start at depth 0, and items are taken from the front, so the crawl is breadth-first and the reported depth is the number of link hops from the start. Each Markdown link resolves to a list of candidate paths: the first is scheduled and the rest are kept as its alternatives. A 404 hands the item to its next candidate at the same depth, so a fallback never counts as another hop, and a URL is scheduled once, because a second arrival only merges alternatives into the entry already waiting. Each item is handled in a fixed order: decode the URL to a bundle-relative path; drop it unless the path is valid and ends in markdown; stop with an error if the byte budget is already spent; fetch it root-bounded, inside the fetch semaphore and under a deadline; on a 404 hand it to its next candidate and on any other error mark it blocked; keep the file, report progress and stop expanding it once the depth limit is reached; then schedule the first candidate of each Markdown link it contains at depth plus one. A file whose links were never expanded, because the depth limit stopped it, stays expandable on click. The crawl reports each file as it loads and the viewer redraws from the files found so far, but not on every file: after the first build the next one waits for one and a half times the current count, so the number of rebuilds grows with the logarithm of the file count. The first build is fresh, every later one grows the graph in place so node positions are kept, and declared decks are applied on each rebuild, so a deck appears with its first page and its members are appended as they load. The crawl refuses several things: only Markdown is fetched and followed, and any other referenced file becomes an unloaded placeholder node; only same-origin URLs inside the bundle root are fetched, with no credentials, query or fragment, so a link that escapes the root is never scheduled; every URL is scheduled once, so a failing candidate is replaced by an alternative rather than retried forever; dot-directories are skipped and an invalid bundle path is dropped before any fetch; at most 8000 scheduled URLs and 128 mebibytes of text, and reaching either stops the crawl with an error instead of returning a partial bundle; and at most four fetches run at a time, with 64 pending and a 30-second deadline on each. A folder opened locally cannot be crawled over the network, so the same idea runs in memory: filterByDepth starts at index.md, else the shallowest Markdown file, and keeps the files within the depth limit, while the rest stay available for on-demand reveal.
svg.text: OKFY · ALGORITHM EXPLAINER
Crawling
One entry file, a queue of links, and a depth limit — nothing outside the bundle
1 · Where the crawl starts
One entry file, and one depth
?start=<file>
the entry file, resolved against the bundle folder
index.md
the default when ?start is absent, on another origin, or outside the folder
?depth=N
how many link hops to prefetch; absent, all or inf means every level
?levels=N
the same limit under an alias
The start is checked against the bundle root before anything is queued, so a start outside it ends
the crawl at once, with nothing loaded.
2 · The queue
depth 0
depth 1
depth 2
index.md
a.md
b.md 404
c.md
b2.md
next candidate
Breadth-first, with alternatives
Take from the front of the queue, so the reported depth is the
number of link hops from the start.
Each link resolves to a list of candidate paths: the first is
scheduled, and the rest are kept as its alternatives.
A 404 hands the item to its next candidate at the same depth,
so a fallback never counts as another hop.
A URL is scheduled once; a second arrival only merges alternatives
into the entry already waiting.
The start is depth 0, and a link found in a depth-d file is scheduled at depth d + 1.
3 · One item, in order
Every item takes the same seven steps
Decode the URL to a bundle-relative path.
Drop it unless the path is valid and ends in .md — the only place a non-Markdown link dies.
Stop with an error if the byte budget is already spent.
Fetch it: root-bounded, inside the fetch semaphore, and under a deadline.
On a 404, hand it to its next candidate; on any other error, mark it blocked.
Keep the file, report progress, and stop expanding it once the depth limit is reached.
Schedule the first candidate of each Markdown link it contains at depth + 1.
A file whose links were never expanded — because the depth limit stopped it — stays expandable on click.
4 · Growing while it loads
The viewer redraws while the crawl runs, but not on every file
the file count when the viewer rebuilds — the first dot is the first build, and each step is 1.5×
The first build is fresh; every later one grows the graph in place, so node positions are kept.
Declared decks are applied on each rebuild, so a deck appears with its first page and grows.
The number of rebuilds therefore grows with the logarithm of the file count, not with the file count.
5 · What it refuses
The bounds that keep the crawl inside the bundle
Only Markdown is fetched and followed; any other referenced file becomes an unloaded placeholder node.
Only same-origin URLs inside the bundle root are fetched, so a link that escapes the root is never scheduled.
Every URL is scheduled once, so a failing candidate is replaced by an alternative, not retried forever.
Dot-directories are skipped, and a path that is not a valid bundle path is dropped before any fetch.
At most 8000 scheduled URLs and 128 MiB of text; either one stops the crawl with an error, not a partial bundle.
Four fetches at a time, 64 pending at most, and a 30-second deadline on each.
A folder opened locally cannot be crawled over the network, so the tool applies the same idea in memory:
filterByDepth keeps the files within the depth limit, and the rest stay available for on-demand reveal.
